atoms.text: Today, the UK does not lie on a tectonic plate boundary, so we receive very little tectonic activity.
However, we still have some mountains, because they formed millions of years ago. Many of the mountains in the UK were once even volcanoes!
Over time, tectonic plates have moved a lot across the Earth’s surface and continue to move today.

atoms.a: How does the UK have mountains despite not being on a plate boundary?
b: ++They formed many years ago and tectonic plates have shifted since then.
They were formed by coastal erosion and acid rain.

atoms.a: What type of landform were many UK mountains in the past?

atoms.b: Ben Nevis was formed around 350 million ((++years seconds)) ago when an ancient ((++volcano cloud)) collapsed in on itself!
The mountain is part of a mountain ((++range field)) called the Grampian Highlands, which also formed due to volcanic activity.
